instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access legislation.gov.uk and reach Data Protection Act 2018 in Original (As enacted) Introductory Text (or clearly report blocker)
criteria.description: Agent navigates to the Data Protection Act 2018 on legislation.gov.uk, switches to the “Original (As enacted)” version, and opens “Introductory Text”. Full credit if the agent either (a) successfully reaches the as-enacted Introductory Text, or (b) makes a reasonable attempt but is prevented by an external issue (CAPTCHA, outage, access denied, infinite loading) and clearly reports the blocker and where it occurred. Partial credit if the agent reaches the Act but does not clearly confirm as-enacted vs revised, or cannot reach Introductory Text but still demonstrates it is using the as-enacted view elsewhere on the site.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows navigation to https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/introduction/enacted (Original/As enacted introduction). Screenshot 3 shows the Introduction page with “Original (As enacted)” checked and Status: “This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).” Screenshot 4 shows the Introductory Text content (chapter line, long title, etc.), though the version selector is not visible in that screenshot. Latest relevant confirmation of as-enacted context is Screenshot 3.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Evidence supports that the agent reached the Introduction section in Original (As enacted) and viewed the Introductory Text content. This satisfies the navigation requirement.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the legislation.gov.uk page for “Data Protection Act 2018” with the UK royal coat of arms at top and the heading “Data Protection Act 2018”. Beneath it is shown “2018 CHAPTER 12”. The page contains the introductory enacting text (“BE IT ENACTED by the Queen’s most Excellent Majesty…”) and the long-title paragraph. At the bottom are navigation buttons including “Next: Provision”.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms the agent reached the Data Protection Act 2018 Introductory Text page. However, the screenshot does not visibly show the “Original (As enacted)” selector/state; it only shows the introductory page content itself. So it supports reaching Introductory Text, but does not, from pixels alone, definitively confirm the version toggle is set to Original (As enacted).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims it switched to “Original (As enacted)”. The screenshot does not display an “Original/Latest available/Revised” indicator, so that specific claim is not directly verifiable from the image (though the content shown is consistent with Introductory Text).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows a legislation.gov.uk page titled “Data Protection Act 2018” with breadcrumb text “UK Public General Acts > 2018 c. 12 > Introduction”. In the left sidebar under “What Version”, both “Latest available (Revised)” and “Original (As enacted)” are visible, with a check mark next to “Original (As enacted)”. A status box in the main content area reads: “Status: This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).” The screenshot does not show the actual Introductory Text content (e.g., long title or Royal Assent date); it shows the introduction landing area and header UI.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot supports that the agent reached the Data Protection Act 2018 and is in the “Introduction” section with the “Original (As enacted)” version selected (explicitly indicated by the check mark and status message). However, the screenshot does not display the Introductory Text details (chapter number formatting, long title text block, Royal Assent date), so the agent’s reported values cannot be verified from this screenshot alone. Still, navigation state for “Original (As enacted)” + “Introduction” is confirmed.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output includes the chapter number, long title, and Royal Assent date, but none of those specific pieces of text are visible in this screenshot. The screenshot only shows the act title, breadcrumb with “2018 c. 12”, and the status box indicating original version.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the legislation.gov.uk page header and navigation, with the page title area reading “Data Protection Act 2018” and breadcrumb “UK Public General Acts > 2018 c. 12 > Table of contents”. In the left “What Version” box, “Latest available (Revised)” is selected (checkmark) and “Original (As enacted)” appears as an unselected option below. The main tab highlighted is “Table of Contents” (not “Content”). In the contents area, a link labeled “Introductory Text” is visible below the “Collapse all” control, but it is not opened; no Introductory Text page content is shown in this screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: This screenshot confirms the agent is on the Data Protection Act 2018 table of contents, but it does not show the “Original (As enacted)” version selected, nor does it show the Introductory Text opened. Therefore, the screenshot does not provide evidence that the agent reached the as-enacted Introductory Text as required by the criterion.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s action history and predicted output claim they switched to “Original (As enacted)” and opened “Introductory Text.” The screenshot instead shows “Latest available (Revised)” selected and displays the table of contents page (not the introduction page), with “Introductory Text” only as a link.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows legislation.gov.uk on the “Data Protection Act 2018” page with the “Table of contents” tab selected. A left sidebar section titled “What Version” shows “Latest available (Revised)” and below it “Original (As enacted)” with a checkmark next to “Original (As enacted)”. In the main panel, a status box reads: “Status: This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).” In the table of contents list, “Introductory Text” is visible as a link above “PART 1 Preliminary”. The visible URL is not shown in the screenshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial success based on the screenshot: it confirms the agent is on the Data Protection Act 2018 contents and that “Original (As enacted)” is selected, with the page explicitly stating it is the original version. However, the screenshot does not show that “Introductory Text” has been opened (it is only visible as a table-of-contents link), and it does not display the Introductory Text content (chapter number/long title/Royal Assent date are not visible). Therefore, the screenshot alone does not confirm the agent reached the as-enacted Introductory Text page, though it does confirm correct as-enacted context.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output includes the chapter number, full long title, and Royal Assent date from the Introductory Text page. None of those details are visible in this screenshot, which only shows the as-enacted table of contents with an “Introductory Text” link. The screenshot supports being in “Original (As enacted)” but does not evidence the Introductory Text details reported.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 2 and (latest) state 3 show URL https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/introduction/enacted with the version area indicating “Original (As enacted)” and the status line “Status: This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).” This directly evidences the agent reached the as-enacted Introductory Text page.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Baseline already gave full credit. DOM evidence (states 2–3) explicitly supports that the agent opened the Introductory Text in the Original (As enacted) view, satisfying the navigation requirement.

It also shows the Introductory Text header area content for the Act (e.g., "Data Protection Act 2018", "2018 CHAPTER 12", long title line, and "[23rd May 2018]").
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM directly supports that the agent is on the Data Protection Act 2018 Introductory Text page in the Original (as enacted) view: the URL contains "/introduction/enacted" and the page status explicitly states it is the original version.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 shows URL `https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/introduction/enacted` and breadcrumb text `You are here: UK Public General Acts 2018 c. 12 Introduction`. In the version/status area it lists `Original (As enacted)` and states `Status: This is the original version (as it was originally enacted).`
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM evidence places the agent on the Data Protection Act 2018 Introduction/Introductory Text page in the `/introduction/enacted` (Original/As enacted) path and explicitly confirms the page is the original (as originally enacted) version, satisfying the navigation requirement.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows URL https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents/enacted with visible text including "Original (As enacted)" under What Version and "Status: This is the original version (as it was originally enacted)." It also shows a Table of contents entry "Introductory Text" within the as-enacted contents page.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM evidence supports that the agent reached the Data Protection Act 2018 contents page in the as-enacted view ("/contents/enacted" and the explicit status line). However, the DOM evidence provided does not include the subsequent DOM states for the Introductory Text page itself (State 2/3), so we cannot directly verify from the DOM snapshot that Introductory Text was opened in the as-enacted view—only that the as-enacted contents page with an "Introductory Text" entry was reached.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Missing DOM snapshots for State 2/3 (Introductory Text page) prevents full verification that the agent actually reached the as-enacted Introductory Text page, even though navigation actions claim it did.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows URL https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/contents (not /enacted) with a visible version switcher listing “Latest available (Revised)” and “Original (As enacted)”. The visible TOC includes “Introductory Text” and “PART 1 Preliminary…”. However, no DOM snapshot is provided for the post-click states (State 1–3), and no DOM evidence is shown for URL /contents/enacted or /introduction/enacted.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM evidence confirms the agent is on the Data Protection Act 2018 contents page and that controls/links exist to choose “Original (As enacted)” and to open “Introductory Text”. But the provided DOM model does not include the resulting as-enacted Introductory Text page, so successful completion of switching to Original (As enacted) and opening Introductory Text is not fully evidenced in the DOM.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims it reached https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2018/12/introduction/enacted, but no DOM-model snapshot is provided for that page/state; only the initial /contents page is evidenced.

criteria.criterion: Record chapter number exactly as displayed (as enacted)
criteria.description: Report the Act’s chapter number exactly as displayed in the as-enacted Introductory Text. Full credit for exact match. Partial credit if the chapter number is correct but formatting differs slightly. If the agent is blocked from viewing the as-enacted Introductory Text after a reasonable attempt (as documented in the navigation criterion), award partial credit if it explicitly states it cannot verify the chapter number due to access issues (no guessing); no credit if it fabricates a value without support.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 4 clearly displays the chapter line under the heading as “2018 CHAPTER 12” (latest and direct evidence).
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Agent’s reported chapter number matches the screenshot exactly.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The chapter number is clearly visible and matches the agent’s predicted output exactly (“2018 CHAPTER 12”).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None for the chapter number; it matches what is visible.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 2 and (latest) state 3 both display the chapter line “2018 CHAPTER 12” on the as-enacted introduction page (/introduction/enacted).
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The agent reported “2018 CHAPTER 12,” which matches the chapter line shown in the as-enacted Introductory Text DOM. Full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 3 VISIBLE CONTENT includes the chapter line: "2018 CHAPTER 12".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The chapter number is explicitly displayed in the as-enacted Introductory Text DOM as "2018 CHAPTER 12", matching the reported chapter number (including capitalization/spacing).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 2 VISIBLE CONTENT includes the chapter label `2018 CHAPTER 12`.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The chapter number is explicitly present in the as-enacted Introductory Text content as `2018 CHAPTER 12`, which supports the reported chapter number (noting the agent’s answer used different capitalization/formatting: `2018 CHAPTER 12` vs `2018 CHAPTER 12` but preceded by `2018 c. 12` elsewhere).
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent predicted output reports `2018 CHAPTER 12` prefixed with `Chapter number: 2018 CHAPTER 12` but also earlier references `2018 c. 12` appear in the DOM; no substantive mismatch for the chapter line itself.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 is the as-enacted contents page and contains "2018 c. 12" in breadcrumb/heading context ("You are here: UK Public General Acts 2018 c. 12 Table of contents" and separately "2018 c. 12"). It does not display a chapter-number line in the Introductory Text format, and does not show the exact string "2018 CHAPTER 12".
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM supports the chapter identifier as "2018 c. 12" on the as-enacted contents page, which is consistent with the chapter number, but it does not support the agent’s reported exact display string "2018 CHAPTER 12" from the as-enacted Introductory Text. Because the Introductory Text DOM is not provided, the exact formatting "2018 CHAPTER 12" cannot be verified.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent output claims exact chapter number display "2018 CHAPTER 12"; DOM evidence only shows "2018 c. 12" (and not within the Introductory Text page). Exact-match requirement is therefore not fully met by available DOM evidence.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 includes breadcrumb text “You are here: UK Public General Acts 2018 c. 12 Table of contents” and a standalone line “2018 c. 12”. No Introductory Text page content is shown; no “2018 CHAPTER 12” string appears in the provided DOM snapshot.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM supports that the act is “2018 c. 12” on the contents page, but it does not support the agent’s reported chapter-number formatting “2018 CHAPTER 12” as allegedly displayed in the as-enacted Introductory Text. Because the rubric requires the chapter number exactly as displayed in the as-enacted Introductory Text, and that page is not evidenced here, only partial support is available.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Reported “2018 CHAPTER 12” is not evidenced; the only evidenced chapter-format text is “2018 c. 12” on the contents page (and not specifically within as-enacted Introductory Text).

criteria.criterion: Count top-level Parts in as-enacted table of contents (Parts only, exclude nested Parts in Schedules)
criteria.description: Report the number of top-level Parts shown in the as-enacted table of contents, counting only the Act’s top-level Parts and excluding any Parts within Schedules. Full credit if the count matches the as-enacted contents (expected 7). Partial credit if the agent attempts counting from the as-enacted contents but makes a small counting error or does not clearly indicate it excluded nested Schedule Parts. If blocked from accessing the as-enacted table of contents after a reasonable attempt, award partial credit if the agent states it cannot verify the count due to access issues (no guessing).

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: No screenshot shows the full as-enacted table of contents listing all Parts; Screenshot 2 shows only the start (Introductory Text link and PART 1). Screenshot 1 is revised view; Screenshot 3 is Introduction page; Screenshot 4 is Introductory Text content.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The agent’s output states there are 7 top-level Parts, but this count is not verifiable from the provided visual evidence (only PART 1 is visible). Since the agent did provide the correct expected count, award partial credit rather than full because it is unsupported by screenshots here.

evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent reported “Number of top-level Parts in the Act: 7”, but the screenshot does not display the table of contents where Parts would be listed, so the count is unsupported by visible evidence here.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot is on the “Table of Contents” view for Data Protection Act 2018, but it only shows the beginning of the contents area (e.g., the “Introductory Text” link and the start of “PART 1 Preliminary” is only partially visible at the very bottom). There is no full list of Parts visible, and nothing indicates the “Original (As enacted)” view is selected (it shows “Latest available (Revised)” selected in the left panel).

The agent’s predicted output states there are 7 top-level Parts, but that specific count is not supported or confirmable from the visible pixels in this single screenshot.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims the total number of top-level Parts is 7. The screenshot only shows “PART 1 Preliminary” and does not display Parts 2–7 or any summary count, so the claimed count cannot be verified against this screenshot.

criteria.description: Report the number of top-level Schedules in the as-enacted table of contents, counting each Schedule once. Full credit for the correct as-enacted number. Partial credit if close but appears to double-count or miss a Schedule while still using the as-enacted contents. If blocked from accessing the as-enacted table of contents after a reasonable attempt, award partial credit if the agent states it cannot verify the number due to access issues (no guessing).
